messages:
From: Morgan Pierce <morgan.pierce@greenfieldbank.com>

Cc: it-security@greenfieldbank.com
Date: 2027-03-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Regulated addenda & subprocessor residency for planned pilot

Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we align internal approvers for a Q2 pilot, InfoSec and Legal asked for a few specific artifacts so we can scope procurement and controls:

- Can Redwood provide a GLBA addendum for commercial banking customers, and a BAA (HIPAA) template if needed?
- We need a clear list of subprocessors and the countries where data may be processed (residency/cross-border).
- Any differences between Hosted API and Dedicated deployments re: data residency and audit logging.
- A short redline-ready DPA (or a clearly annotated diff) so our legal team can speed review.

Attaching the preliminary vendor assessment template they requested. If possible, can you confirm whether Redwood supports an on-prem / VPC deployment that can be air-gapped for certain proof-of-concept workloads?

Ideally we’d have answers and the DPA diff by end of next week (3/16) so we can keep the procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Morgan Pierce
Director, Vendor Risk Management — Greenfield Bank
morgan.pierce@greenfieldbank.com
[Attachment: vendor-assessment-template.xlsx (XLSX)]
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-03-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regulated addenda & subprocessor residency for planned pilot

Hi Morgan —

Really appreciate the clear asks and the timeline. Short answers up front: yes to a GLBA addendum template, yes we can provide a BAA template for healthcare-scoped pilots, and we will deliver a redline-ready DPA diff. I’ve attached a brief note outlining the high-level differences between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments with respect to residency and audit logging.

Quick clarifications so we deliver exactly what you need:
1) For the DPA diff, do you want us to propose the majority of text changes or would Legal prefer a mark-up against Greenfield’s standard DPA?
2) For residency, is the ask simply country-level disclosures for subprocessors, or do you require region-specific guarantees (e.g., EU-only processing for a particular dataset)?
3) If an air-gapped on-prem option is required, we’ll need to understand the vendor acceptance criteria (SLA expectations, support windows, and patching cadence).

Looping in Ben (sales lead on this account) so we can coordinate pricing/rollout. I’ll also bring Laura from compliance in on the next note to confirm the subprocessor list and what we can commit to contractually.

Next steps: I’ll send an internal packet to Ben/Laura this afternoon with the draft attachments and a suggested DPA diff. If it helps, we can do a 30-min alignment call with your InfoSec on Wednesday.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com

—Rachel

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Phil Dobbs <phil.dobbs@secpartners.io>
Date: 2027-03-11T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Regulated addenda & subprocessor residency for planned pilot — Greenfield Bank (action items)

Team —

I reviewed Morgan’s assessment and sketched a recommended contract posture and a short technical FAQ we can include with the DPA diff. Summary below:

1) Subprocessors & residency
- Canonical subprocessor list can be provided; at present we have processing nodes in US (primary), GCP EU-west (backup for EU customers), and a small infra partner in Singapore for APAC routing.
- For Greenfield’s pilot we can commit to US-only processing if they contract for Dedicated capacity or Private VPC via our Private offering. Hosted (shared) customers cannot receive a contractual global-residency guarantee due to multi-tenant routing.

2) Addendum templates
- GLBA addendum: we have a standard text that covers customer financial data handling, logging, and incident notification windows.
- BAA: available, but only applicable if customer data is PHI; scope must be explicitly scoped in SOW.

3) Audit logs & controls
- Dedicated and Private expose token-level audit logs and a per-route latency/cost breakdown suitable for audit. Hosted exposes aggregated logs; we can provide SOC2 reports (Type II) and runbook excerpts.

4) DPA redline approach
- I’ll produce a redline-ready DPA diff that (a) highlights fields Greenfield typically pushes on (subprocessor list, data export restrictions, audit rights, breach notification timelines) and (b) offers Redwood’s preferred language for residency and subprocessors.

5) On-prem / air-gapped
- We can do a limited air-gapped Private deployment, but it’s an engineered engagement: minimum term/commitment, on-site support windows, and separate patching cadence. I’ll flag a few runbook items they need to accept.

I’ve attached the completed InfoSec questionnaire (filled) and a short one-pager for the legal DPA negotiation playbook. Phil — if you can review the technical answers and validate we didn’t overclaim on controls, that would be great; I included him to help sign off quickly.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: security-questionnaire-filled.xlsx (XLSX)]

Subject: Re: Regulated addendum pathing & subprocessor residency — Greenfield Bank pilot (materials attached)

Morgan —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal alignment we’re attaching the DPA diff and the completed InfoSec questionnaire. Highlights and next steps:

- Attached: redwood-dpa-diff.pdf (annotated DPA with proposed language for GLBA/BAA addenda), security-questionnaire-filled.xlsx, and a short addendum-pathing note that shows what we can commit to for Dedicated and Private.
- Residency commitment: for the pilot we can offer US-only processing if Greenfield contracts Dedicated capacity or requests a Private VPC deployment (we’ve summarized the minimal contractual language in the DPA diff). Hosted/shared accounts cannot receive contractual residency guarantees due to underlying multi-tenant routing.
- Subprocessors: canonical list included; we can commit to advance notice and an annual update in the contract. Specific subprocessor country disclosures are provided in the redlined DPA (see section 4.2).
- BAA: included as an appendix to the DPA diff for reference — if the pilot will touch PHI, let us know and we’ll scope it into the SOW.
- On-prem / air-gapped: we can support as an engineered engagement. Ben will follow up with pricing/commitment options and expected onboarding timeline.

If Greenfield is comfortable, I’ve included a DocuSign link to the DPA diff for signature routing to speed Legal review: https://www.docusign.com/sign/XYZ-GB-1123

Proposed next steps:
1) Greenfield Legal: review DPA diff and indicate preferred redlines (we’re happy to take your mark-up).
2) If residency/Dedicated is desired for the pilot, confirm capacity commitment and Ben will produce a pricing addendum.
3) Schedule a short call with InfoSec (we suggest 30 minutes) to walk the questionnaire answers — Phil is available to join if you want a third-party technical review.

We’ll plan to hold pricing for the Dedicated pilot proposal for two weeks from the date of proposal.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com
